series.label: pipeline warm-up

series.hypothesis: an unmodified engine reproduces iteration-0 throughput and is REJECTED by the merge gate (no improvement)

series.label: Batched decode
series.mechanism: one stack traversal per step for all co-resident decodes
series.hypothesis: decode serialization is the whole iteration-0 gap: advancing all co-resident sequences through ONE batched 66-layer traversal (weights read once per step, per-layer Python paid once) instead of one traversal per sequence multiplies aggregate decode throughput at conc 8

series.label: Triton NVFP4 dequant
series.mechanism: bit-exact one-pass dequant kernel under every routed-expert GEMM
series.hypothesis: on-demand expert dequant TRAFFIC, not launch count, dominates the batched decode step: eager dequant_nvfp4 moves ~750 MB of int64/fp32 temporaries per expert w13 (0.689 ms), ~44 hit experts x 64 MoE layers ~ 3.1 s/step ~ the whole step wall at batch 8; a bit-exact one-pass Triton kernel (0.089 ms/expert, 7.7x) multiplies decode AND prefill throughput with zero numeric change

series.label: Concurrency 8 to 64
series.mechanism: batched decode fed 64 co-residents instead of 8
series.hypothesis: decode is weight-bandwidth-bound: batch 8->64 amortizes non-expert weights 8x; MoE expert traffic grows only ~4.5x (top-6-of-256 coverage saturates ~200 experts), netting 3-8x aggregate

series.label: Grouped NVFP4 MoE GEMM
series.mechanism: routed-expert GEMMs computed directly on packed NVFP4 bytes, one grouped launch per matrix
series.hypothesis: post-exp-0002 the batched decode step is still MoE-bound, not attention-bound: moe_experts is 645.9 ms of the 918 ms step at B=8 (70%) because every hit expert still materializes 112 MB of bf16 weight and re-reads it in cuBLAS (~225 MB HBM round-trip per expert to serve 1-2 rows) plus ~11 eager launches per expert and a per-layer unique().tolist() sync; a grouped Triton GEMM that dequantizes packed bytes in-register (bit-equal LUT, all 256 patterns verified) and runs all (token,slot) pairs in one launch per matrix deletes the traffic AND the loop, multiplying decode and prefill throughput

series.label: Engine batch 64
series.mechanism: server admission-cap default 8 -> 64 so bench conc-64 actually co-resides in one batched step
series.hypothesis: Ranked-next (1) from the exp-0005 profile row, cited per the STEP-B ruling: every bench row to date INCLUDING the 15.3 best ran the engine at internal batch 8 — server.py --max-batch defaults to 8 and the worker serve_cmd never overrides it (verified live on the exp-0004 process table) — so timeboxed(conc=64) concurrency queued at the HTTP layer instead of reaching the engine. series.label: Pooled batched attention
series.mechanism: decode attention core batched over per-layer KV batch pools — one ~20-op chain per layer instead of per row

series.label: Hardware FP4 dequant
series.mechanism: grouped NVFP4 GEMM dequant swapped to the Blackwell cvt.rn.f16x2.e2m1x2 hardware convert — bit-identical outputs, 1.21x both kernels
series.hypothesis: Post-exp-0009 the 61.4 tok/s cycle (133.4 s per 64-seq cohort) is floored on BOTH terms by the SAME two kernels: the exp-0009 profile puts the grouped NVFP4 GEMM at 93% of prefill CUDA (13.5 ms/layer at T=736 after BLOCK_M 32 -> prefill term 75.5 s), and the exp-0005 kernel table puts the same kernels at 179 ms GPU of the B=64 decode step (_gate_up_silu 128.5 + _down_scale 50.9) — the largest GPU block remaining after exp-0007/0008 deleted the attention/sconv storms. Inside these kernels the per-element in-register dequant chain (_e2m1 bit construction: ~10 int-ALU ops + fp32 mul + RTNE, re-run for the full weight tile per (expert, n-tile, k-chunk, m-chunk)) is the floor; exp-0009 reduced the NUMBER of dequant passes, this diff reduces the COST of each: cvt.rn.f16x2.e2m1x2 (PTX 8.6, the CUDA-13 __nv_cvt_fp4x2_to_halfraw2 form) converts both nibbles of a packed byte in ONE hardware instruction via tl.inline_asm_elementwise (pack=1 — pack=4 silently mispacks when a thread owns <4 elements, probe-proven). Because e2m1->f16 and f16->fp32 are exact, the fp32 value*scale mul and RTNE-bf16 round are unchanged, so full-kernel outputs are BITWISE identical to the accepted engine (exp-0008 class): torch.equal TRUE at both launch configs on identical inputs, and the TF gate reproduces exp-0003..0009's output exactly including the disagreements sample. Measured on synthetic checkpoint-shape packs (t_moe_cvt/t_moe_cvt_sweep logs): 1.21x whole-kernel at BOTH operating points — decode-scale T=64 9.99 -> 8.29 ms, prefill-scale T=736 13.5 -> 11.0 ms and T=1018 14.0 -> 11.6 ms at (32,128,128) — best config per scale unchanged, so the exp-0009 dispatch constants stay. Native-FP4 tensor-core MMA (tl.dot_scaled, the bigger rewrite ranked next by exp-0009) was tried FIRST and is dead on Triton 3.6/sm_103a: MLIR assert in TritonGPUAccelerateMatmul for every bf16 x e2m1+e4m3-scale shape (t_ds_probe log) — the remaining floor after this diff is the convert pipe (~2.5 cvt-class ops/element for f16->f32 and RTNE-bf16, inherent to any bit-equal dequant), which only a native-MMA CUDA/CUTLASS port or Triton upgrade can delete.

series.label: CUDA-graphed decode
series.mechanism: batched decode step captured into per-device CUDA graphs — static buffers, B padded to max_batch, monotone 512-bucket key length, one argmax readback
series.hypothesis: Adjudicated attack (a) from the exp-0011 in-situ profile row (insitu_phase_exp0011_2026-07-30.log: dec_enq 107.1 s of dec_wall 108.4 s over 256 steps at ~64 rows — host enqueue = 98.8% of decode-step wall): delete the per-step host dispatch (~6k eager Python/torch/Triton enqueues over the 66-layer pooled traversal) by capturing the step into per-device CUDA graphs replayed on static buffers. Staticization: B padded to max_batch via a dedicated pool scratch slot (identically-configured dead rows so colliding scratch writes carry identical bytes; kv.py +1 row/page), global key length padded to a monotone 512-bucket high-water L_pad (recapture <= 32/lifetime; only the current bucket ever replays after a new capture, keeping shared per-device graph pools in capture order), layer-2's bf16 expert reference loop as an eager island on LIVE rows only (dead rows in its per-hit-expert GEMM batches would couple live-token bits to scratch history through row counts), bincount -> searchsorted in moe_experts_packed (bit-identical integer offsets; bincount's data-dependent output size is a hidden device sync that invalidates capture), page allocation hoisted to a page-boundary host check, and the 64 per-row argmax .item() syncs collapsed to ONE batched argmax readback. MEASURED (in-process A/B, one resident load, 64 reqs, /workspace/logs/t_graph_ab_exp0012_2026-07-30.log): graph run1 == run2 BITWISE across a mid-run 512->1024 bucket recapture (the t_b3-adapted determinism arm); warm graphed step 473.0 ms vs eager 476.6 ms (+0.76% at ISL 220-500). The premise was WRONG in an instructive way: exp-0011's host-enqueue share measured the host WALL, not GPU idleness — the kernel profile of the graphed step (t_graph_profile_exp0012_2026-07-30.log, ISL~700-772, 459.7 ms/step CUDA total) shows the step was ALREADY GPU-bound at near-parity with dispatch: _gate_up_silu 184.9 + _down_scale 81.5 = 266.4 ms/step (58%) in the grouped packed-NVFP4 GEMMs (dequant-ALU-bound at M~1-2 rows per hit expert, ~5.7x off the ~47 ms/step weight-traffic roofline) plus ~128 ms/step (28%) of matmul-contiguous direct_copy on the pooled attention K/V gathers (260 copies/step). Bench prediction is therefore ~flat; the row locks in the dispatch floor — the substrate every kernel-side win needs so host cost cannot re-emerge as kernels shrink (at 200 ms/step of GPU the eager path's ~450 ms host wall would dominate; the graphed path's host cost is ~the island only) — and its kernel table adjudicates the ranked-next attacks: (1) decode-shape grouped NVFP4 GEMM (dequant-once staging or the CUDA/CUTLASS native-FP4-MMA port, D5 roadmap / exp-0010 DEADENDS) worth up to ~220 ms/step, (2) copy-free two-shape attention with fused rel-bias (attack #5) worth up to ~120 ms/step.

series.label: Fused decode attention
series.mechanism: two-shape flash-decode Triton kernel reads K/V in place from the batch pools — in-kernel ring/page indexing, fused rel-bias, zero gather/contiguity copies
series.hypothesis: Ranked attack (2) from the accepted exp-0012 row's graphed-step kernel table (t_graph_profile_exp0012_2026-07-30.log: ~128 ms/step, 28% of the 459.7 ms GPU-bound step, is matmul-contiguous direct_copy on the pooled attention K/V gathers — 260 copies/step — plus the [B,H,1,L] score/bias/softmax intermediates inside 'rest'): attn_decode_batch_pooled materializes K = pool.k[slots] / V = pool.v[slots] (134 MB each per SWA layer at B=64) then re-copies them matmul-contiguous, while the KV-traffic roofline for ALL 66 layers' decode attention is ~2-3 ms/step. This diff replaces steps #4-#6 of the pooled core with ONE Triton flash-decode kernel per layer (shared @triton.jit body, IS_SWA constexpr — D4's two-shape attention w/ fused rel-bias): program (b, kv_head) processes its REP GQA heads against K/V read IN PLACE from kv.SwaPool (ring geometry recomputed in-kernel from pos, decode_batch_ctx #1 math) or the GlobalPool flat page pool (through the torch-built masked flat indices), rel bias gathered in-kernel from the tiny precomputed rel-logit mix rel[b,h,clamp(dist,0,E-1)] and zeroed out of band, tau round-trip kept in torch (commutes with the gather at identical rounding points), dead slots excluded by selection (-1e38), fp32 online softmax, probs downcast bf16 for the PV dot, fp32 accumulate, one bf16 round on store. Appends, projections, sconv, and the whole prefill path are untouched. MEASURED (t_graph_ab, one resident load, same protocol as the exp-0012 log, /workspace/logs/t_graph_ab_exp0013_2026-07-30.log): warm graphed step 473.0 -> 322.7 ms (-150 ms, 1.47x) at ISL 220-500 — an UNDERSTATEMENT of the bench point (ISL~736: SWA rings full at 512, the deleted gathers larger); eager arm 476.6 -> 361.2 ms; eager-vs-graph rows now 64/64 bitwise (flash masked lanes contribute exactly zero at any padded length). Determinism: graph run1 == run2 BITWISE across the mid-run 512->1024 recapture (t_b3 arm); t_fused_attn fused-twice bitwise on both shapes, maxdiff vs the eager chain 0.00195 (1-2 bf16 ulp) over ring-wrap/beyond-extent/scratch-row edges.

series.label: Batched group prefill
series.mechanism: co-admitted prompts prefill as one right-padded length-sorted batched traversal — expert dequant amortized across rows
series.hypothesis: The accepted cycle is now PREFILL-term-dominated: exp-0013's accepted 89.7 tok/s block is 448 reqs / 639.5 s = 91.4 s per 64-cohort = ~61 s serial prefill (~67%) + ~30 s decode, because exp-0007..0013 rebuilt the decode step while every prefill still walks the 66 layers once PER SEQUENCE. Prefill is GPU-bound in the grouped packed-NVFP4 GEMM (exp-0009 profile: 93.4% of prefill CUDA pre-BLOCK_M-fix), whose per-(expert, n-tile, k-chunk, m-chunk) full-tile dequant is paid once per sequence: at T~736 only 17-24 rows/expert fill one BLOCK_M-32 m-chunk, so 64 serial walks pay ~64 full-matrix dequant passes per layer per cohort, each serving ~17 rows. Right-padding co-admitted prompts into ONE batched walk (the exp-0009 DEADENDS groundwork: admission groups under a 4 GiB padded-scores budget, per-row states seeded through the unchanged per-seq slice calls, causality isolating real rows from pads) raises rows/expert to ~G x 17 and pays the walk's Python once. Two refinements were forced by measurement: (a) unsorted FCFS packing wasted ~33% of all per-token work on pad rows (measured 1.19x) — stable LENGTH-SORTING the admits before packing (partition stays a pure function of the admitted lengths; running-list order untouched) recovers it; (b) an idle-edge 150 ms accumulation window in EngineLoop keeps a retiring cohort's replacement arrivals from fragmenting into tiny first groups. MEASURED (one resident load, N=64 canonical-ISL-class prompts 500..999, sorted groups [45,19]; t_prefill_batch_exp0014_sorted2 log): serial 75.9 s vs grouped 58.4 s = 1.30x on the prefill term; in-situ through the live server (exp0014_http_ab2 log): 1.15x at 32 concurrent (arrival-race fragmentation bounds it below the engine-level ceiling). NOT expected to reach the groundwork's 1.5-2x projection: exp-0009/0010 already cut the per-pass dequant cost the projection assumed, and attention's padded-score share grows with G. prefill_heavy is untouched by design: an 8K pair exceeds the scores budget (every group is a singleton -> bitwise the per-seq path) and at ~192 rows/expert its dequant is already amortized — the win is specific to short-ISL admission cohorts.
